# REDULTRON CORE 3.0 — Release Package and Integration Plan

**Package status:** reproducible ZIP is generated by GitHub Actions; production runtime and Android device are not certified.  
**Source of truth:** the exact Git commit used by the package workflow.  
**Distribution target:** installable Progressive Web App (PWA) bundle for Android/Chrome and desktop browsers.

## What this package contains

- `jarvis/index.html` — PWA interface.
- `jarvis/manifest.webmanifest` — install metadata and icon declarations.
- `jarvis/sw.js` — service worker and bounded cache/offline behavior.
- `jarvis/diagnostics.js` and declared icon assets.
- This release note, Android install guide, commit SHA, and SHA-256 checksum generated by the workflow.

The ZIP includes `INSTALL-ANDROID.md`. This is a **PWA ZIP package**, not an Android APK. Install it by deploying the files to the configured HTTPS origin and using Chrome's install action. An APK would require a separate, reviewed Trusted Web Activity/Capacitor build and signing pipeline.

## Integration inventory (evidence-first)

The following workstreams are related but must not be merged blindly. Each PR needs its own conflict, dependency, test, and security review. The package workflow does not claim these open PRs are already part of `main`.

| Workstream | PR | Current known state | Release treatment |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Correlated, sanitized Python Core auth diagnostics | #472 | Merged per GitHub record; CI/prod verification must be checked on the current deployed SHA | Include only when present in the package's source commit; verify runtime separately |
| Production deployment approval gates | #431 | Open draft in the latest inspected record | Keep production deploys blocked until review, required checks, and Environment reviewers are confirmed |
| Python Core upstream auth status diagnostics | #430 | Open draft in the latest inspected record | Review alongside #472 to avoid duplicate/overlapping behavior |
| Fail-closed owner-secret length guard | #447 | Open, non-draft; checks reported passing in its PR description | Review overlap with #431 before merging either |
| Python Core secret synchronization | #393 | Open draft; blocked by missing Render API credential / secret parity evidence | Do not sync or rotate secrets in package workflow |
| Integration registry | #461 | Open draft; registry tests reported passing in its PR description | Merge/review separately; do not treat registry status as live proof |
| Bounded Python health retries | #365 | Open, non-draft; checks reported passing in its PR description | Check whether newer main already contains equivalent logic before merging |
| PWA legacy cache cleanup | #415 | Closed/merged in prior listing | Verify deployed service-worker/cache version with a live probe |

PR statuses can change; refresh GitHub before release approval.

## Required pipeline

1. **Source integrity:** package must be built from a recorded commit SHA; never mix unreviewed PR heads implicitly.
2. **Static tests:** run `npm test` on Node 22.
3. **PWA contract:** validate manifest JSON, standalone display, start URL/scope, icons, app shell, and service worker.
4. **Artifact:** create a ZIP and SHA-256 checksum; retain the commit SHA in the artifact.
5. **Review:** inspect workflow logs and artifact contents before distribution.
6. **Deployment:** separate, explicit approval-gated workflow only. Building an artifact must never deploy or mutate production.
7. **Runtime certification:** independently verify Worker health, Python health, authenticated hybrid execution, search provider/fallback, D1/KV/DO, and agent execution on the same deployed SHA.
8. **Device verification:** test PWA installation, update activation, voice/microphone ownership, and offline navigation on a real Android device.

## Release acceptance gates

- [ ] Repository CI passes on the exact package SHA.
- [ ] Package workflow succeeds and ZIP/checksum artifact is available.
- [ ] Manifest and all declared icons are present.
- [ ] Service worker syntax and expected cache marker are checked.
- [ ] No credentials, tokens, or environment files are included in the bundle.
- [ ] Deployment approval policy is enforced in GitHub Environment settings.
- [ ] Worker deployed SHA is identified and matches the reviewed release.
- [ ] Authenticated Python Core probe returns HTTP 200, `engine=python-edge-hybrid`, `fallbackEngaged=false`, and `hybridPythonCoreExecutionVerified=true`.
- [ ] Live Search provider attribution and fallback behavior are tested.
- [ ] Android PWA install/update and offline navigation are tested.

A ZIP artifact is not a production-ready release until all applicable gates are checked with fresh evidence. Do not label an unverified integration as operational.
